narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To explain that test-optional colleges report higher average test scores than test-required colleges because students selectively submit their higher scores, inflating the school's statistics.

units.meaning: Test-optional reported average scores exceed test-required at every sampled year.
accepted_routes: Reported averages are higher for test-optional than test-required.
At each shown year, test-optional scores are slightly to clearly higher.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both series visible; test-optional line stays above test-required at labeled years.
units.temporal_anchor: Second, their average test scores are higher.
units.reviewer_question: Should the higher series be labeled TEST-OPTIONAL despite the entity column swap?

units.meaning: Both series rise from 1994 to 2010; test-optional increases by 140.
units.computation: 2010 value minus 1994 value for each series.
accepted_routes: Both averages trend upward over the period.
Test-optional climbs from 990 to 1130; test-required from 980 to 1100.
Scores increase over the sixteen-year window.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Start and end values visible for both lines.
units.temporal_anchor: Second, their average test scores are higher.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video show the overall upward trend, or only the level difference?

units.meaning: The gap is largest at 2010: test-optional 1130 vs test-required 1100.
accepted_routes: The two series diverge most at the final year.
The 2010 gap is wider than earlier gaps.
units.reviewer_question: Is highlighting the largest endpoint gap optional or required?

units.meaning: Test-required drops from 1125 in 2006 to 1100 in 2010, while test-optional holds at 1130.
accepted_routes: Test-required declines in the final period.
Test-optional stays flat while test-required falls.
The late drop in required scores widens the gap.
units.visual_evidence_rule: 2006 and 2010 values for both series visible.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video call out the late test-required drop?

units.meaning: Selective submission: higher-scoring students submit, inflating test-optional reported averages.
accepted_routes: Students self-select which scores to submit.
Only higher scores are sent, raising reported averages.
Selective submission inflates the school's average statistics.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Narration or on-screen text explains selective submission mechanism.
units.temporal_anchor: Each student knows all of his or her scores and individually decides whether to submit them.
units.reviewer_question: Is the causal mechanism required even though the table has no submission data?

optional_valid: Show the 1998, 2002 and 2006 sampled years as intermediate confirmation.
Note that the two lines remain close until 2010.
unsupported_to_avoid: Claiming the gap grows every year; it does not.
Using percentages, counts or submission rates absent from the table.
Stating the selective-submission mechanism is proven by the chart data.
notes: Entity column appears swapped; units use series column to match intent. Values are cited from table rows with matching series.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
